notes: §1985:XIV.3.6.4 GR1 governs only "a receiving communication device ... oriented to a fixed line size". This implementation has no such device: docs/CONFORMANCE.md (Communication devices row) and McsStore.Transmit make every device (a destination with no deliverTo, a terminal) the file <name>.out oriented to variable-length messages, each complete message written whole as one line, so the antecedent is never true and GR1c's "Excess characters ... are not truncated" holds trivially. Probe s1 (classes c, d, e, f): a 150-character group message (100 A, 50 B) SEND WITH EMI to DEV answers 00 and DEV.out holds all 150 characters on one line; the witness prints SEND DONE.

next.reason: 1985: "When a receiving communication device (printer, display screen, card punch, etc.) is oriented to a fixed line size"; 2023: "SEND now sends a message to a message server run unit; no communication device or line-size rules remain". The 1985 Communication module SEND to devices is gone. The 2023 SEND is a message-server statement with no line-size rules, and DISPLAY/COLUMN candidates cover other features.
